exposure: Enrollment in a midwifery-led Weight Intervention Group (specialised antenatal management programme)
outcome: Pregnancy care (implementation of local high BMI guidelines including nutritional/weight gain advice, regular weighing, lactation consultant referrals, third trimester anaesthetic review, ultrasound)
cohort: The study included 1115 pregnant women with singleton pregnancies and a Body Mass Index (BMI) >30.
finding: Women with high BMI enrolled in a specialised antenatal management programme received increased care and had superior breastfeeding initiation rates, but engagement was poor, and no significant differences were noted in antenatal or postnatal complications, mode of birth, or neonatal outcomes.
mod_finding: No significant difference was noted in the Caesarean rate or overall mode of birth between the intervention and control groups.
